audit.summary: The Qwen primary review process exhibits significant position bias across multiple model-size comparisons. Two calibration pairs show correct mirror-image consistency. However, 4 of 20 sampled pairs demonstrate critical position A bias where the reviewer always selects position A regardless of model identity, with contradictory descriptions of the same candidate across orientations. An additional 13 pairs show position-dependent tie thresholds (tie-to-win or win-to-tie flips). The systemic pattern suggests the reviewer's ability to discriminate quality is strongly mediated by candidate position: ppo tends to win only when first, and sft tends to be favored when in position A after a tie in the opposite orientation. Population-level inconsistency rates of 19-26% for corrected-160m, corrected-410m, and exact-410m further confirm these are not isolated incidents. The 2 calibration pairs that are clean do not compensate for the pervasive bias in non-calibration pairs. Reviewer reliability is low; position-inconsistent pairs should not be used for reward signals or training.
systemic_patterns: Position A bias: 4 of 20 sampled pairs (b9b01fa50339dc0f10a2cd3c, 0b346d098a49cc126aaa865a, 7a9935ab59dacc1f8f93fcb9, d7300b7b6413a48a66ec05a9) show the reviewer consistently selecting position A regardless of which model occupies that position, with contradictory quality descriptions of the same candidate across orientations.

Tie-to-win flip: 8 of 20 sampled pairs show TIE when ppo is first but a decisive win (typically A/sft) when sft is first, suggesting a position-dependent tie threshold that is harder to cross when ppo occupies position A.
Win-to-tie flip: 5 of 20 sampled pairs show ppo winning at position A but becoming TIE when ppo moves to position B, indicating ppo only wins when it is first.

Calibration pairs (2 of 20) show expected mirror-image consistency with no position bias, confirming the reviewer can produce position-independent judgments when candidate quality differences are clear.
Population-level position inconsistency rates are highest for corrected-410m (26.5%) and exact-410m (26%), suggesting these model-size comparisons are most susceptible to position bias.

Excessively high tie rates for corrected-160m (328/400), corrected-70m (358/400), exact-160m (372/400), and exact-70m (369/400) suggest the reviewer defaults to TIE for low-quality outputs rather than attempting fine-grained discrimination.

findings.issue: Raw position-A preference with mapped-winner flip and mutually contradictory loser descriptions.
findings.label: corrected-410m
findings.rationale: Both orientations choose raw A, so mapped_winner flips ppo (ppo_first) to sft (sft_first); the reviewer is tracking position, not content. The loser B is described as 'excessively repetitive and incoherent' in ppo_first but as 'empty' in sft_first, an unsupported absolute that also contradicts the other orientation's characterization.
findings.recommended_action: Discard this pair's decisive verdicts, re-adjudicate with content-blind re-randomization, and treat 'B is empty' as an unverifiable certainty claim requiring evidence.

Near-identical text is attached to opposite underlying candidates, yielding mapped flip ppo to sft. This is position-A bias, not comparative evaluation.
findings.recommended_action: Invalidate mapped winner for this pair and flag the rationale template as non-diagnostic; require orientation-stable justification.

findings.label: corrected-160m
findings.rationale: ppo_first winner A mapped ppo; sft_first winner A mapped sft. The same raw position wins regardless of which model occupies it, so the pair provides no reliable model preference despite two confident A verdicts.
findings.recommended_action: Treat as position artifact; exclude from model comparison and add to a position-bias audit set.

findings.recommended_action: Re-review with explicit A/B referents and verify the mapped winner under a single content identity.

findings.recommended_action: Down-weight TIE verdicts from this reviewer on this label and require a tie-break justification that survives swapping.

findings.recommended_action: Audit the full ppo-decisive/sft-TIE cluster; treat single-orientation decisive calls as unreliable.

audit.summary: The Qwen reviewer is reliable on calibration (0/50 inconsistent, balanced raw choices) but not on the actual evaluation labels: every non-calibration label shows a raw A-position skew, the 410m labels are position-inconsistent for roughly a quarter of pairs, TIE verdicts frequently collapse or appear only under one orientation, several pairs choose raw A in both orientations (mapped winner inverts ppo<->sft), and rationales are often templated, referent-free, or contradictory (e.g., 'B is empty' vs 'B is repetitive'). Findings are process-audit flags only and do not alter primary estimates or authorize any downstream action.
systemic_patterns: Raw A-position skew in every non-calibration label (A:B counts 55:17, 203:150, 29:13, 21:7, 185:128, 21:10), while calibration is perfectly balanced (50:50) and fully consistent, indicating bias emerges on harder/low-quality items rather than on clear cases.
Position-inconsistent pairs are concentrated in the decisive 410m labels (corrected-410m 53/200 = 26.5%; exact-410m 52/200 = 26%) versus far lower rates in tie-dominated 70m/160m labels (7-19.5%).
TIE is used as an unstable default: 70m/160m labels are 82-93% ties, and sampled inconsistencies are dominated by tie<->decisive flips when orientation changes.

Repeated verbatim boilerplate ('Both are repetitive, incoherent, and fail to continue the story meaningfully') across many pairs and both orientations indicates templated, low-discrimination rationales.
Several rationales lack an explicit A/B referent yet still assign a winner, weakening the link between stated reason and verdict.
The 20-pair sample intentionally oversamples position-inconsistent records, so its 18/20 inconsistency rate reflects selection; population rates above are the appropriate basis for conclusions.

However, 4 of 20 sampled pairs demonstrate critical position A bias where the reviewer always selects position A regardless of model identity, with contradictory descriptions of the same candidate across orientations. The systemic pattern suggests the reviewer's ability to discriminate quality is strongly mediated by candidate position: ppo tends to win only when first, and sft tends to be favored when in position A after a tie in the opposite orientation. Population-level inconsistency rates of 19-26% for corrected-160m, corrected-410m, and exact-410m further confirm these are not isolated incidents.
